label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: all complete True, pending max 4.0, failures 0, server errors 0.0, pool timeouts 0, other edges 0

A.rule: no failed deliveries and pending stayed low

report.summary: No delay observed in the window: outbox publications keep pace with arrivals, deliveries all succeed in about 71 ms, and the oldest undelivered age never exceeded about 1.2 s.

findings.claim: The outbox is not backing up: 480 arrivals vs 479 publications, pending 1-4, no failures.
findings.reason: Arrivals minus publications is 1 and the run settled. Failed stayed 0 and pending ranged 1-4.

findings.claim: Oldest undelivered event age stayed between 0.22 s and 1.18 s, consistent with the 1 s poll interval.
findings.reason: The maximum age of 1.18 s is about one outbox poll interval (1000 ms).

findings.claim: Delivery attempts were fast and all succeeded on attempt 1; no retries, errors or slow consumer.
findings.reason: 479/479 SUCCESS, p95 77.7 ms, max 80 ms, with the consumer's own handler time negligible.

findings.claim: The database and connection pool were not contended.
findings.reason: Zero acquisition timeouts, pending borrowers 0, and no blocking in 75 samples.

limitations: Only a 150 s window at low steady load was observed; the delayed notifications may have occurred outside it.
The consumer is a test fixture, so real notification provider latency is not covered.
next_checks: Re-run the diagnostics over the time period when customers reported late notifications.
Inspect the downstream notification provider and the consumer's own pipeline for queueing delays.

alternatives.reason: The tools only measured the delivery to the consumer endpoint, a local fixture, not any downstream notification channel.
alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness occurs downstream of the consumer (push/SMS/email provider) or on the customer device.

alternatives.reason: The window had a steady 3.2/s load with no stress, so it may not reproduce the customers' conditions.
alternatives.hypothesis: The problem occurred at a different time or under higher load than this 150 s window.

report.summary: Within the window, outbox deliveries kept pace with transfers and were delivered quickly with no failures, retries, pool pressure or DB blocking. The late notifications are not reproduced here.

findings.claim: Outbox publications kept pace with committed transfers; the backlog stayed tiny and short-lived.
findings.reason: 480 arrivals vs 479 publications, pending 1-4, oldest undelivered age max 1.18 s, failed 0.

findings.claim: All 479 deliveries succeeded on the first attempt with about 71 ms latency, dominated by consumer auth time.
findings.reason: 479 SUCCESS, no errors or retries; p95 77.7 ms, max 80 ms.

findings.claim: Transfer API, DB pool and DB locks show no stress that could delay the outbox.
findings.reason: No 5xx, p99 0.25 s; pool pending 0 with no timeouts; 0 blocked sessions in 75 samples.

limitations: Window is only 150 s; the intermittent lateness customers report may fall outside it.
Consumer is a test fixture; real downstream notification channels were not observed.
